name: kill
description: Kill someone here.

target_id.description: Exact id of who here died.

name: leave_party
description: Make a party member stop travelling with the player.

target_id.description: Exact id of the party member leaving.

name: direct
description: End the turn and give notes to the narrator. Call this last, once per turn. Include the answer or result, its known reason, and facts needed for the next choice. Share only facts the player can know now. Apply world changes through the other tools before calling direct.

text.description: Brief factual notes for the narrator to phrase. Answer each question in the player action. Include the result, its known reason, and details needed for the next choice. For a request or warning, give what the person wants and the reason they share. Use facts the player can know now. Identify claims and unknown reasons as such. Keep every outcome consistent with tool results.

name: enter
description: Bring a cast member into the scene.

target_id.description: Exact id of a cast member not already here.

name: leave
description: Send a cast member out of the scene.

name: join_party
description: Make a person here travel with the player. Set `terms` when the player hires them to work, also someone who already travels with the player: the worldsmith writes their sheet at the end of the turn, and nothing more happens this turn. Leave `terms` empty for someone who only comes along.

target_id.description: Exact id of who here joins or is hired.

terms.description: Empty when they only come along. When the player hires them to work: what for and on what terms, as agreed.

name: reveal
description: Make a hidden entity here known to the player. HIDDEN HERE lists what the player has not found: call this before you tell a hidden thing.

target_id.description: Exact id of something hidden here.

name: change_hindrances
description: Add hindrances to the actor, remove hindrances, or do both.

gained.description: Hindrances the actor now carries. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

lost.description: Hindrances the actor no longer carries.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

name: gain_item
description: Give the actor an item they pay for.

name.description: The item's name. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

bulky.description: True when the item takes much space to carry.

breaks.description: How many times the item can break before it is broken until repaired.

cost.description: Credits paid; most items cost ₡1. Use 0 for a thing found or given.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

name: drop_item
description: Take an item from the actor permanently.

item_id.description: Exact id of an item the actor carries.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

name: repair_item
description: Repair a broken item of the actor.

item_id.description: Exact id of an item the actor carries, a ship function, or an item in THE HOLD while the ship is here.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

name: spend
description: Pay the actor's credits for a thing that is not an item and not a repair, or pay someone with `to_id`.

why.description: What the credits pay for, in a few words.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

to_id.description: Exact id of whoever gets the credits: a crew member keeps them, anyone else, such as a hire paid up front, takes them. Null when they pay for a thing.

name: ship_upgrade
description: Upgrade one ship function for the player.

function_id.description: Exact id of a ship function. The player pays ₡10.

upgrade.description: What the upgrade is. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

name: lose_hold_item
description: Take an item out of the ship's hold while the crew is away: a raid, an impound or a theft. Call this once for each item.

item_id.description: Exact id of an item in THE HOLD.

why.description: What takes it: a raid, an impound or a theft. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

name: defend
description: Break a carried item or a ship function. The hit becomes a hindrance.

item_id.description: Exact id of a carried item, or of a ship function.

hindrance.description: What the hit leaves behind after the item takes it, as a brief hindrance that the engine removes at the next scene. Empty for an item that breaks with no harm. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

name: next_scene
description: Open the next scene: with nothing set when this one reaches a stopping point. Set `pursuit` instead when the player has left this place. Set `complication` instead to test for bad luck here: on 1-2 the trouble comes, on 3-4 only its signs.

pursuit.description: Where the player is going, in their own words. Empty to offer the way on.

by_ship.description: True when the crew flies its own ship there with `pursuit`. The ship stays where it is docked otherwise.

complication.description: The trouble that bad luck would bring here, and why: the engine rolls a d6 for it. Empty otherwise.

name: bring_in
description: Bring a new operator into the crew after the lead died; the worldsmith writes them.

who.description: The new operator in the player's words.

name: roll
description: Roll only to avoid a risk. The engine checks the dice and asks the player to commit, unless `committed` is set; then it rolls and reads the result.

what.description: The attempt, in a few words the player reads.

risk.description: What they take in full on a disaster: an injury, a loss, a cost or an alarm. Name it before the roll; set `harm` when it hurts them, and then name the injury. A roll with no risk is not a roll. A helper shares it, with `harm`, `deadly` and `setback_hurt`. Say it in one short phrase, never more than 100 characters.

deadly.description: True when `risk` is death. A disaster then kills them, and they do not get `risk` as a hindrance. A setback then maims them.

harm.description: True when `risk` hurts them: an injury or a wound. `risk` then names the injury itself, such as `Burned hands`, never the event that causes it. The engine writes a disaster's `risk` on the sheet as a hindrance and a setback as a brief one, and the player can break gear to turn a disaster into a brief one. False for a loss, a cost or an alarm.

setback_hurt.description: With `harm`: the lesser hurt a setback leaves, one step down from `risk`, such as `Bruised ribs`. The engine writes it as a brief hindrance. Empty writes `Minor hurt`. Name it in three or four words, never more than 48 characters.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a hired party member here who acts. Null for the player.

skill.description: The skill to roll. Empty rolls the plain d6.

helped.description: The circumstance that helps: an advantage the story has already set up for this action, such as a position won earlier, a tool made for this task, or help from a party member who is not hired. Never scenery, what makes the action possible at all, or the skill the die already counts. Empty otherwise.

actor_id.description: Exact id of the hired member who helps.

hindered.description: Why the helper is hindered. Empty when nothing hinders them.

skill.description: The skill the helper rolls. Empty rolls the roll's own `skill`. A d6 when their sheet lacks it.

helped_by.description: The hired member who helps. They roll their skill die and share the risk. Null when nobody helps.

hindered.description: Why the actor is hindered. Empty when nothing hinders them.

committed.description: True only when the player's own words for this action name this danger and accept it, such as 'I jump even if I fall'. A bare 'I shoot him' accepts nothing. That the story told the danger before is never enough.

name: job
description: Work for the crew. With `find` the engine rolls the d6 of the SRD. With `finish` it raises one skill for each hired member, pays each operator d6 credits, and asks the player which skill they raise.

verb.description: `find` looks for work. `take` records agreed work, or new terms for the open job. `finish` closes the job.

where.description: Where the player looks for work, in a few words. Required with `find`.

terms.description: Who wants the work and what the work is, as agreed. Name no credit figure: each operator's pay is a d6 rolled when the job is finished. Required with `take`.

raises.description: With `finish`, one per living hired member. The player picks their own raise.

actor_id.description: Exact id of a living hired member.

skill.description: The skill that the job used for this member. A skill that is not on their sheet is added at d8.

name: raise_skill
description: Raise the skill the player chose after a job.

skill.description: The skill the player named for their raise after a job; a new one starts at d8.
